transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-26 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Lina Gomez (Redwood); Rachel Ortega, Tom Black, Priya Shah (Valencia)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining. quick checkin today — renewals, capacity, and the region asks. rachel can you kick us off on where you stand on the renewal?
[00:18] Rachel Ortega: yeah thanks maya. overall pretty happy, our team wants to renew but we also need to expand — underwriting spikes in q4 mean we need more headroom. curious about dedicated capacity options and multi-region.
[00:35] Tom Black: hi team, from infra perspective latency in ap-southeast is a problem right now. we see 120-150ms tail with the hosted endpoints during peak, so looking at either a dedicated pool in ap-southeast or routing to a closer region.
[00:52] Samir Patel: got it. we talked last quarter about a reserved pool for your peak windows. we can size GPUs based on token/sec and concurrent sessions — do you have new concurrency numbers?
[01:10] Rachel Ortega: yes, for underwriting we spike to ~600 concurrent inference sessions for 1-2 hours, average request length 350 tokens, bursty.
[01:27] Samir Patel: ok that helps. for 600 concurrent at 350 tokens, rough calc suggests a dedicated pool of 6x A100-equivalent or 8x T4-class depending on quantization. we'll run a more precise sizing.
[01:45] Priya Shah: quick security note — we need to make sure KMS integration works with our HSM provider, audit logs must be tamper-evident, and data residency for eu-west is required for some lines of business. also SSO via SAML and SCIM for onboarding.
[02:05] Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll include the security pack. lina, can you confirm we have docs for HSM/KMS flow and audit log retention?
[02:13] Lina Gomez: yes we do, i'll share the security pack link after the call; it includes our SOC 2 attest, KMS integration patterns, and audit log export examples.
[02:25] Rachel Ortega: thanks. what's the cost delta for dedicated in two regions vs single region?
[02:33] Samir Patel: generally dedicated clusters add a baseline monthly commit. multi-region doubles some fixed costs but we can do smart routing where only critical traffic hits the ap-southeast cluster. we can also suggest autoscaling/burst capacity to reduce commit.
[02:52] Tom Black: on routing — can Redwood do weighted routing by latency and cost, with automatic fallback to hosted during failover?
[03:02] Samir Patel: yes that's a core pattern — smart routing can route by region, cost tier, or latency SLO. fallback to a compatible model variant is supported. note: model variant swapping may change latency a bit.
[03:18] Rachel Ortega: hmm model variant swap — how big is the difference? we can't afford regressions in quality for claims triage.
[03:28] Samir Patel: fair, we'll flag that. tradeoff example: a quantized 4-bit variant lowers cost ~40% but may slightly change hallucination profile; we'll run evals on your prompt set during the pilot.
[03:45] Maya Chen: ok next piece is timeline — you mentioned q4 peaks; what's your desired live date for the expanded regions and capacity?
[03:55] Rachel Ortega: ideally mid-October for ap-southeast, with eu-west earlier if possible — some EMEA underwriting goes live Sept 20.
[04:05] Lina Gomez: we can try to prioritize eu-west first. Samir, do we have capacity lead times?
[04:13] Samir Patel: provisioning Dedicated pools typically 2-3 weeks if we have capacity. for private or on-prem it can be longer. for hosted dedicated we can often do it in 10-14 business days if contract and PO are in place.
[04:30] Tom Black: contract — we want a 24-month term to lock pricing, but also a clause to increase capacity mid-term. how flexible is that?
[04:39] Maya Chen: we can do a 24-month extension with scaling addenda; we'll include step-up options and pre-negotiated unit prices. i'll draft an addendum showing pricing tiers.
[04:51] Priya Shah: another security ask: can audit logs be forwarded to our Splunk with encryption-in-transit and at rest?
[04:59] Samir Patel: yes, we support syslog/HTTPS sinks and can integrate with Splunk HEC. logs are encrypted in transit and at rest; we'll show the sample config.
[05:12] Rachel Ortega: great. about the benchmark — can Redwood run a staging bench with our prompt set and simulate concurrent bursts? we'd like latency p95 under 200ms for underwriting workflows.
[05:25] Samir Patel: yes, we can run a benchmark in staging. ideally we get your representative prompt set and a small test harness. we can simulate the 600 concurrent burst and measure p50/p95/p99.
[05:40] Tom Black: we'll share prompts and sample traffic shape. expected turnaround?
[05:46] Samir Patel: 7-10 business days after we get artifacts and credentials for the staging workspace.
[05:55] Rachel Ortega: ok that fits. maya, do you have any concerns from a pricing standpoint?
[06:02] Maya Chen: main ask is to keep unit price predictable — with a 24-month term we'll hold pricing, and the dedicated commit reduces per-token cost. i'll include cost examples in the addendum.
[06:14] Priya Shah: for KMS/HSM — we need to review key rotation policies and the support for customer-managed keys. can we get a tech note?
[06:23] Lina Gomez: yes, samir and i will include the KMS tech note. samir, maybe add the HSM flow and any limitations.
[06:30] Samir Patel: will do. note: some on-prem HSM integrations require extra work; if you're using cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) integration is straightforward.
[06:43] Rachel Ortega: we use a hybrid approach, so we'll list specifics.
[06:48] Tom Black: curious, any recommendation on quantization strategy for our workload? we care about token throughput but not at cost of NLU accuracy.
[06:57] Samir Patel: for underwriting prompts we usually recommend 8-bit quant for production — good throughput gains with minimal quality loss. 4-bit can be evaluated but only after prompt-set evals. we'll include quantization recommendations per model.
[07:12] Maya Chen: i'll make sure the proposal contains two scenarios: conservative (8-bit + dedicated) and aggressive (4-bit + more batching) with cost/latency tradeoffs.
[07:23] Rachel Ortega: about data residency — for eu-west we need data not to leave EU for that LOB. can Redwood guarantee?
[07:32] Lina Gomez: with Dedicated and Private deployments we can enforce region-only routing and local storage. we'll document data flows.
[07:40] Priya Shah: great. also SSO — we need full SCIM support for groups.
[07:45] Samir Patel: SCIM + SAML are supported. small note: initial provisioning latency for SCIM can take a few minutes; we'll provide best practices.
[07:57] Tom Black: any blockers on our side for a staging bench? we need to share prompts, service account, and a traffic simulator.
[08:06] Rachel Ortega: we'll get that to you by EOD Friday.
[08:10] Maya Chen: perfect. recap — we will: 1) send pricing and 24-month addendum, 2) Samir runs capacity sizing and staging benchmark planning, 3) Lina shares security pack and KMS/HSM note, 4) Valencia sends prompts and compliance list.
[08:27] Rachel Ortega: yes that sounds right. one question — are there any competitors we should be aware of in the proposal review? we have internal folks looking at Bedrock and Anthropic.
[08:38] Maya Chen: noted, we'll include a short competitive positioning doc. we also can show performance benchmarks vs open models.
[08:46] Priya Shah: last question: if we increase capacity mid-term do we get pro-rated credits?
[08:53] Maya Chen: yes typically we pro-rate additional reserved capacity from the date of change; details will be in the addendum.
[09:00] Tom Black: thanks everyone.
[09:03] Maya Chen: thanks all — lina will follow up with the security pack, samir will schedule the sizing workshop, i'll send pricing. we'll target follow-up next week after Valencia shares prompts.
[09:15] Rachel Ortega: thanks, bye.

Note: transcript has occasional transcription artifacts; speaker overlaps and short crosstalk present. References to KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" in recordings and product names like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes appear as "Redwood Dedicate" in auto-transcript.
